item.title: Two men charged with cocaine trafficking in St Julian's
item.description: Solomon Haile, 32, and Mohammed Eisa, 25, pleaded not guilty to cocaine possession and trafficking within 100 metres of a youth-gathering space, along with cannabis offences against Haile. The pair were arrested on Saturday in Paceville after Eisa was seen disposing of a sachet with a white substance, and text messages on their seized mobiles suggested drug trafficking; neither requested bail.

item.title: Heritage Malta warns of fake ticket website impersonating the agency
item.description: Heritage Malta has filed a police report over a fraudulent website, heritagemalta.mom, impersonating the agency and selling fake admission tickets to museums and historical sites. The agency was alerted by a customer who paid for tickets but never received them, and urged the public to check the address carefully and buy only through heritagemalta.mt or at the sites themselves.

item.title: Man denied bail over €4,000 warehouse burglary
item.description: Paul Spagnol was remanded in custody over a €4,000 burglary from a warehouse in Mrieħel, after police caught him inside the building on Saturday night. Officers found a bag with gloves, a saw, pliers and about €4,000 in a pouch. Bail was refused because the prosecution raised concerns over evidence tampering and the accused's ability to comply with bail conditions.

item.title: Survey: 45% lack confidence in government's economic management
item.description: The second Esprimi Budget Barometer 2027 found 45% of respondents have no confidence in how the government is running the economy, against 32% who do, a net deficit of 13 percentage points. Separately, the higher tourist eco-contribution was named the least welcome Budget measure by 33% of those surveyed, with only 8% welcoming it, while energy subsidies and the Mater Dei emergency department expansion topped the list of popular measures.

item.title: Malta among nine EU countries falling short on 2030 climate targets
item.description: The European Commission said Malta and eight other member states risk failing their 2030 emissions targets and must submit corrective action plans within three months. The Commission report, issued at the COP31 summit, said Malta, Germany and Ireland show the largest projected gaps to target and that "Malta is projected to emit more in 2030 than in 2005".

item.title: Four Romanian men jailed over Valletta pickpocketing spree
item.description: Elvis Adir, 25, and Florin Rambo Mamolescu, 28, received three years and four months in prison each for admitting to 11 pickpocketing thefts in Valletta, while Martinelli Bruno Adir, 18, and Manix Baboi, 21, were jailed for three years each. Valletta police and CID officers identified the four suspects within three days of the first reports, Home Affairs Minister Glenn Bedingfield said.

item.title: Momentum urges Caruana to publish 2018 population-growth report
item.description: Momentum called on Finance Minister Clyde Caruana to publish the roughly 300-page report he said he prepared in 2018 warning about the strains of Malta's population boom on housing, hospitals, schools and roads. Caruana has not shown the report to the Times of Malta, though former prime minister Joseph Muscat said he requested it and received it in late 2018. Momentum leader Arnold Cassola said publishing it was the least Caruana could do.

item.title: Malta among EU states where house prices rose slower than incomes
item.description: Eurostat figures comparing the house price-to-income ratio between 2015 and 2025 show Malta's ratio fell, while the EU average rose 6.8%, placing Malta with Italy, Cyprus, Sweden and France in the group where incomes grew faster than prices. The data does not mean prices fell, and the report notes affordability remains a concern for residents.

item.title: Fiscal Advisory Council urges shift to productivity-driven growth
item.description: The Malta Fiscal Advisory Council recommended that government shift its economic growth model, warning that reliance on expanding the labour force threatens medium-term public finance sustainability. It called for productivity-boosting measures, high-quality capital investment and better allocation of state resources, noting that output per worker has stayed low despite growth. The council endorsed forecasts of real GDP rising 4.1% in 2026 and 3.8% in 2027.

item.title: Labour Party buys Birżebbuġa club after court ordered it to vacate
item.description: The Labour Party has purchased its Birżebbuġa Labour Club, party president Alex Sciberras announced, more than a year after a Constitutional Court ruling found the party's earlier takeover of the property had breached the owner's fundamental rights and ordered it to vacate.

item.title: Man killed in Baħar iċ-Ċagħaq boat crash identified; injured 14-year-old remains stable
item.description: The man who died when a boat ran aground off Baħar iċ-Ċagħaq on Sunday evening has been identified as 48-year-old Keith Caruana from Mellieħa, whose 14-year-old son Ben was also injured. Sources said the fatal injuries were compatible with being thrown onto the rocks. A third man, 44 and from Cospicua, is also being treated at Mater Dei Hospital. Ben remains in intensive care but in a stable condition, his mother Yanika Rizzo said, thanking the caller who raised the alarm.

item.title: €60 million reverse osmosis plant planned for Ħal Far
item.description: The Water Services Corporation is to invest around €60 million in a new reverse osmosis plant in Ħal Far, which will increase capacity to produce 40 million litres of potable water a day. The project was unveiled by Energy and Environment Minister Miriam Dalli.

item.title: 'You're a liar': animal rights activists clash in court over cat cafe
item.description: Carmen Coleiro, who managed the cat cafe at the St Vincent de Paul long-term care facility from 2016, was accused of lying by animal rights activist Romina Frendo during the compilation of evidence on Monday. The court heard allegations of starving cats, filthy conditions and misuse of funds at the cafe, which was shut down in 2023, with the activist claiming animals continued to be admitted despite reports of deaths.

item.title: Tourist eco-contribution increase is least welcome Budget measure, survey finds
item.description: In the second release of the Esprimi Budget Barometer 2027, the expansion of Mater Dei Hospital's emergency department and the continuation of energy subsidies were the most welcomed measures, named by 41% and 42% of respondents respectively. item.title: One dead and two in critical state after boat hits reef off Baħar iċ-Ċagħaq
item.description: A man has died and a second man and a 14-year-old boy are in a critical condition after the boat they were travelling in struck a reef off Baħar iċ-Ċagħaq on Sunday evening. Police were alerted at around 7.15pm that a boat had run aground on the reef known as Is-Sikka s-Safra, with passers-by reporting flares lit on board. The three victims, two men and a boy, were transferred by a Civil Protection Department vessel, treated on the beach by medics and then taken to Mater Dei Hospital, where their condition was described as serious. The Civil Protection Department said the rescue was carried out in close coordination with the Armed Forces of Malta, the police and Mater Dei Hospital emergency staff, and asked the public to avoid the hospital except in genuine emergencies.

item.title: Man, 59, arrested over €4,000 theft from Mrieħel warehouse
item.description: A 59-year-old resident of San Ġwann was arrested after allegedly stealing around €4,000 from a warehouse in Triq l-Intornjatur, Mrieħel, on Saturday night. Police were called out at around 9.30pm to a suspected burglary and found a broken window overlooking the warehouse car park, which officers believe the suspect used to gain entry. The man was found inside an office during the search of the building and the money was recovered. Separately, Times of Malta reported that a 59-year-old man was later arrested in the case.

item.title: Pantomime poster outside Parliament vandalised
item.description: The poster for the Bella u l-Bestja pantomime was found vandalised outside Parliament in Valletta early on Sunday morning, the show's author Rodney Gauci said. Gauci claimed the damage was deliberate rather than wind or accident, and said the poster had been cut from the frame advertising the pantomime, which opens at the end of the year. He called the attack "an attack on the art", and a report was filed with the police, who appealed for information.

item.title: €500 maintenance grant for solar water heaters opens
item.description: Applications opened on Monday for a €500 maintenance grant for households that installed a solar water heater under the 2021 government grant scheme at least five years ago. The Regulator for Energy and Water Services said the scheme is aimed at covering servicing costs for systems bought under the 2021 Solar Water Heater Grant.

item.title: Artists hit back at culture minister after claims they think they are 'God's gift to the world'
item.description: Malta's creative community has hit out at Culture Minister Malcolm Paul Agius Galea after he said many artists believe they are "God's gift to the world" and that art should exist within certain "norms". Speaking at the Festival of Ideas, Agius Galea said that artistic expression has to operate within societal norms, and described his first months in office as "presumptuous and dangerous" and "traumatic" while adapting to a profession where creativity is central. Several prominent figures in the sector publicly questioned his understanding of the sector he oversees, calling him unqualified and out of touch with the people who work in it.

item.title: Artists and MEIA hit back at culture minister over remarks on creativity
item.description: Malta's creative community continued to hit out at Culture Minister Malcolm Paul Agius Galea after he described his first months in office as "traumatic" and said art should exist within certain norms. The Malta Entertainment Industry and Arts Association said the minister "does not understand the sector he is responsible for" and that "creativity is not a danger to be contained", while challenging his position on public arts funding. Content creator Kurt Rumbajsa also questioned who was "holding a gun to his head" to keep him in a portfolio he holds in "such high contempt".

item.title: Police recruitment age could rise from 39 to 50, Bedingfield says
item.description: Home Affairs Minister Glenn Bedingfield said the government is considering raising the maximum age for police recruits from 39 to 50, which would allow older and more experienced candidates to join. Recruits joining above the current limit would not qualify for the full 25-year pension arrangement but would receive a pro-rata pension. Around 80 new recruits have started training and are expected to graduate in September.

item.title: Boy, 14, stable after boat struck reef off Baħar iċ-Ċagħaq
item.description: The mother of Ben Rizzo, the 14-year-old who was left in a critical condition when a boat struck a reef off Baħar iċ-Ċagħaq on Sunday evening, said on Monday that his condition had stabilised. Yanika Rizzo shared an emotional message thanking the person who made the "lifesaving call" and urging her son to keep fighting. Ben remains in the Intensive Care Unit. A witness, Charlotte Anne Falzon, separately recounted hearing cries for help and seeing two distress flares before the vessel's lights went out and it fell silent.

item.title: No plans to let early retirees draw pension and work
item.description: Finance Minister Clyde Caruana said there are no plans to allow those who can retire before the age of 65 to receive their pension and work at the same time, saying "you can't have your cake and eat it". The comments add to the government's debate on how to keep the labour force and social security system sustainable as the population ages.
